core_principles.text: Maintain strict whole-body tension throughout the flight phase of a plyometric push-up to ensure the body behaves as a single rigid segment.

common_mistakes.text: Allowing pronounced hip flexion or segmental motion of the body during the flight phase of a plyometric push-up.

specific_findings.text: A 5-degree shoulder-flexion perturbation during the flight phase of a push-up displaces the center of mass from the nominal pendular arc by approximately 0.05 meters for representative anthropometry where body length is 0.60 meters and the initial angle is 12 degrees.

consequences.text: Pronounced hip flexion or segmental motion during the flight phase of a push-up produces deviations from the predicted pendular arc, reducing movement consistency and performance estimation.

source: data\push-up\A Rigid-Body Pendulum Model for Plyometric Push-Up Biomechanic.pdf [part 6/22]

core_principles.text: The initial configuration of the push-up requires the arms to be fully extended and oriented vertically, perpendicular to the floor.

common_mistakes.text: Recreational execution of push-ups often involves minor translational displacement of the ankle at takeoff.

specific_findings.text: For a body mass of 75 kg at hand velocity up to 3.0 m/s, the peak aerodynamic drag force is approximately 0.5 N.
For representative anthropometric arm lengths of 0.7 to 0.9 meters, the upper bound of hand take-off velocity is 3.7 to 4.2 m/s.

consequences.text: Minor translational displacement of the ankle at takeoff alters the effective pivot location and introduces position-dependent errors in biomechanical calculations.

source: data\push-up\A Rigid-Body Pendulum Model for Plyometric Push-Up Biomechanic.pdf [part 7/22]
